reduce_excess_by_one needs binary representations: for each excess index, x = t*a + (1-t)*b where a ∈ S, b ∈ convexHull(S), 0 < t < 1. This follows from convexHull_not_mem_requires_two by grouping points.

Critical for perturbation: strict positivity of weights (0 < w i) enables choosing ε that zeroes out exactly one weight while keeping others positive. The strengthened convexHull_not_mem_requires_two provides this.

reduce_excess_by_one proof sketch: (1) pick d+1 excess indices, (2) get binary reps, (3) direction vectors δₘ=bₘ-aₘ are linearly dependent, (4) perturb along dependence to push one index to a ∈ S, (5) new decomposition has fewer excess indices.
Key subtlety in perturbation: push TOWARD a (the S-element) not b (the convexHull element). This ensures the collapsed index lands in S, becoming non-excess.
